correctness.rationale: The dark space is the sum, over distinct adjacency eigenspaces, of the trap-orthogonal directions. It reduces both terms of the generator. On its orthogonal complement the eigenvalue identity Im(z)||v||² = −gamma |v_0|² rules out any nondecaying eigenvector, so finite-dimensional Jordan blocks do not affect the limit. Only the lower hub/uniform-rim eigenvalue can coincide with a nonuniform Fourier energy, and it is strictly negative. At the collision, the hub eigenvector has rim weight a²=λ/[2(λ−1)] and hub weight b²=1−a²; the degenerate trap projection has squared norm (a²+d)/n. Removing it leaves b²d/(a²+d), exactly as claimed. The negative Fourier energies are distinct, including −2 at the even endpoint. With τ=1 the collision requires n≤8, and exact small-size comparisons leave n=3 and n=8. The uploaded checker and requirements were inspected, not executed. The independent rational Krylov check in /workspace/review-evidence/independent_checks.py reproduced ranks and masses for unit spokes n=3..9, and for n=12 at τ=1/2 (rank 7, mass 2/3) and τ=51/100 (rank 8, mass 0); the general proof, not this finite test, handles all parameters.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The dark hub weight is E_hh−|E_0h|²/E_00. Substitution gives b²d/(a²+d), and at a visible rank-one projector it gives zero. The Fourier-only blocks have E_hh=0. Applying the established single-trap projection identity to those entries yields the survival law by direct substitution, not merely by analogy between two observables.
